Imaging Department

Exam: mpMRI Prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (0.76 ng/mL), prior negative biopsy. Evaluate for clinically significant prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 36.0 mL in volume. The transition zone is unremarkable. In the left peripheral zone at the apex, a focal lesion is identified measuring approximately 9 mm in its greatest dimension. On T2-weighted imaging, the lesion appears as a subtle hypointense area. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates restricted diffusion in this region, with corresponding low signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early arterial enhancement of the lesion, peaking in the late arterial phase and showing washout relative to the surrounding peripheral zone tissue.

IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the left peripheral zone apex with features consistent with PI-RADS 4.

previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 0.7 ng/mL in May 2024, representing a slight increase from previous measurements. Given the persistent low-level elevation and a newly identified PI-RADS 4 lesion on MRI, a prostate biopsy was performed under local anesthesia. The procedure was well tolerated with no immediate complications. The patient was advised to monitor for any urinary symptoms or haematuria.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (01 Jul 2024): Prostate tissue obtained via transrectal ultrasound-guided systematic sampling. Microscopic examination reveals benign prostatic glands and stroma. No malignant cells are identified. The Gleason score is 0+0, corresponding to ISUP grade group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. There is no perineural invasion. The tumour location is peripheral zone, apex left.

Summary: Histological findings across the single available biopsy timepoint remain stable, showing no evidence of prostate carcinoma.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 0.
